Misir Wat (Spiced Red Lentil Stew)

35 minEasyServes 1–4

Prep — Misir Wat on a Fasting Platter

Ingredients by Serving

Ingredient1234
Red split lentils60g120g180g240g
Red onion, chopped40g80g120g160g
Garlic clove, minced½11½2
Ginger, grated⅛ tsp¼ tsp⅜ tsp½ tsp
Berbere spice blend½ tsp1 tsp1½ tsp2 tsp
Tomato paste5g10g15g20g
Vegetable oil or niter kibbeh10ml20ml30ml40ml
Vegetable stock or water200ml400ml600ml800ml
Saltpinch⅛ tsp¼ tsp⅜ tsp

Steps

  1. Warm the oil (or niter kibbeh) in a pot over medium heat. Add the onion and cook 8-10 minutes, stirring, until soft and golden.
  2. Add the garlic and ginger and cook 1 minute until fragrant.
  3. Stir in the berbere and tomato paste, cooking 1-2 minutes until deep red and fragrant.
  4. Rinse the lentils, then add them to the pot along with the stock or water. Bring to a boil.
  5. Reduce heat and simmer, uncovered, 15-20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the lentils are fully soft and the stew has thickened.
  6. Season with salt to taste, thinning with a splash more water if needed.
  7. Serve warm with injera, or over rice as a shortcut.

Tibs (Sautéed Beef with Peppers & Onions)

25 minEasyServes 1–4

Prep — Tibs Sizzling Over Charcoal

Ingredients by Serving

Ingredient1234
Beef sirloin, cut into thin strips130g260g390g520g
Saltpinch⅛ tsp¼ tsp⅜ tsp
Black pepperpinch⅛ tsp¼ tsp⅜ tsp
Onion, sliced30g60g90g120g
Green bell pepper or jalapeño, sliced¼½¾1
Garlic clove, minced½11½2
Ginger, grated⅛ tsp¼ tsp⅜ tsp½ tsp
Berbere spice blend¼ tsp½ tsp¾ tsp1 tsp
Niter kibbeh or butter10g20g30g40g
Rosemary sprig (optional, traditional)¼½¾1

Steps

  1. Pat the beef strips dry and season with salt and pepper.
  2. Heat the niter kibbeh (or butter) in a skillet over high heat until shimmering.
  3. Sear the beef 2-3 minutes, tossing occasionally, until browned outside but still pink in the middle. Remove to a plate.
  4. In the same skillet, add the onion and pepper, cooking 4-5 minutes until softened and lightly charred in spots.
  5. Add the garlic, ginger, and rosemary (if using), cooking 1 minute until fragrant.
  6. Stir in the berbere and a pinch of salt.
  7. Return the beef and any juices to the skillet and toss 2-3 minutes until coated and cooked to your liking.
  8. Serve hot, straight from the pan, with injera or flatbread.

Shiro Wat (Spiced Chickpea-Flour Stew)

30 minEasyServes 1–4

Prep — Shiro Wat Spooned onto Injera

Ingredients by Serving

Ingredient1234
Chickpea flour (or shiro powder)40g80g120g160g
Onion, finely chopped30g60g90g120g
Garlic clove, minced½11½2
Tomato, chopped¼½¾1
Berbere spice blend½ tsp1 tsp1½ tsp2 tsp
Vegetable oil10ml20ml30ml40ml
Water200ml400ml600ml800ml
Saltpinch⅛ tsp¼ tsp⅜ tsp

Steps

  1. Heat the oil in a saucepan over medium heat. Add the onion and cook 5 minutes until soft and translucent.
  2. Add the garlic and cook 1 minute until fragrant.
  3. Add the chopped tomato and berbere, cooking 2-3 minutes until the tomato breaks down and the mixture is deep red.
  4. In a separate bowl, whisk the chickpea flour into the water until completely smooth with no lumps.
  5. Pour the chickpea-flour mixture into the pot, whisking constantly as it heats to prevent clumping.
  6. Bring to a gentle simmer and cook 8-10 minutes, stirring frequently, until thick, glossy, and no longer tastes raw or floury.
  7. Season with salt, thin with a splash more water if needed, and serve hot with injera.

Atkilt Wat (Cabbage, Carrot & Potato Stew)

35 minEasyServes 1–4

Prep — Atkilt Wat on a Mixed Platter

Ingredients by Serving

Ingredient1234
Green cabbage, sliced150g300g450g600g
Carrot, sliced50g100g150g200g
Potato, cubed80g160g240g320g
Onion, sliced30g60g90g120g
Garlic clove, minced½11½2
Ginger, grated⅛ tsp¼ tsp⅜ tsp½ tsp
Ground turmeric⅛ tsp¼ tsp⅜ tsp½ tsp
Ground cumin⅛ tsp¼ tsp⅜ tsp½ tsp
Vegetable oil10ml20ml30ml40ml
Water30ml60ml90ml120ml
Saltpinch⅛ tsp¼ tsp⅜ tsp

Steps

  1. Heat the oil in a wide pan or pot over medium heat. Add the onion, garlic, and ginger, cooking 3-4 minutes until softened.
  2. Stir in the turmeric and cumin, cooking 1 minute until fragrant and the onions are stained gold.
  3. Add the potato and the water, cover, and cook 8-10 minutes until the potato is nearly tender.
  4. Add the carrot, cover, and cook 5 minutes more.
  5. Add the cabbage and salt, cover, and cook 8-10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until tender but the cabbage still has a little bite.
  6. Taste and adjust salt. Serve warm, on its own or alongside a wat.

Doro Wat (Spiced Chicken Stew)

75 minMediumServes 1–4

Prep — Doro Wat Plated on a Full Platter

Ingredients by Serving

Ingredient1234
Chicken thighs, bone-in, skin removed150g300g450g600g
Red onion, finely diced60g120g180g240g
Garlic clove, minced1234
Ginger, grated¼ tsp½ tsp¾ tsp1 tsp
Niter kibbeh or butter15g30g45g60g
Berbere spice blend1 tsp2 tsp3 tsp4 tsp
Tomato paste10g20g30g40g
Chicken stock or water60ml120ml180ml240ml
Hard-boiled eggs1234
Saltpinch⅛ tsp¼ tsp⅜ tsp

Steps

  1. Melt the niter kibbeh (or butter) in a heavy pot over low heat. Add the red onion, cover, and cook 20-25 minutes, stirring every few minutes, until deeply softened and jammy.
  2. Add the garlic and ginger, cooking 2-3 minutes until fragrant.
  3. Stir in the berbere and tomato paste, cooking 2 minutes until the mixture turns deep brick red and smells toasted.
  4. Add the chicken thighs, turning to coat every piece in the spiced onions.
  5. Pour in the stock or water, bring to a gentle simmer, cover, and cook 25-30 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the chicken is cooked through and tender.
  6. Nestle the hard-boiled eggs into the sauce, spooning some sauce over each. Simmer uncovered 5-10 minutes so the eggs soak up flavor and the sauce thickens slightly.
  7. Season with salt to taste. Serve hot with injera.

Key Wat (Spiced Beef Stew)

60 minMediumServes 1–4

Prep — Key Wat on an Injera Platter

Ingredients by Serving

Ingredient1234
Beef stew meat (chuck), cubed150g300g450g600g
Saltpinch⅛ tsp¼ tsp⅜ tsp
Black pepperpinch⅛ tsp¼ tsp⅜ tsp
Red onion, finely diced60g120g180g240g
Garlic clove, minced1234
Ginger, grated¼ tsp½ tsp¾ tsp1 tsp
Niter kibbeh, butter, or oil15g30g45g60g
Berbere spice blend1 tsp2 tsp3 tsp4 tsp
Tomato paste10g20g30g40g
Beef stock or water100ml200ml300ml400ml

Steps

  1. Heat the niter kibbeh (or oil) in a heavy pot or Dutch oven over medium heat. Season the beef with salt and pepper, then brown it in batches, 2-3 minutes per side. Remove to a plate.
  2. In the same pot, add the onion and cook 12-15 minutes, stirring occasionally, until deeply golden and softened.
  3. Add the garlic and ginger, cooking 1-2 minutes until fragrant.
  4. Stir in the berbere and tomato paste, cooking 2 minutes until deep red and fragrant.
  5. Return the beef and any juices to the pot, then pour in the stock or water. Bring to a simmer.
  6. Cover and simmer on low 35-40 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the beef is fork-tender.
  7. Uncover and simmer 5 more minutes to thicken slightly if needed. Season with salt.
  8. Serve hot with injera or rice.

Gomen (Collard Greens with Garlic & Ginger)

30 minEasyServes 1–4

Prep — Gomen on a Vegetarian Sampler

Ingredients by Serving

Ingredient1234
Collard greens, stemmed and sliced150g300g450g600g
Onion, chopped30g60g90g120g
Garlic clove, minced1234
Ginger, grated¼ tsp½ tsp¾ tsp1 tsp
Vegetable oil or niter kibbeh10ml20ml30ml40ml
Water or stock30ml60ml90ml120ml
Ground cumin (optional)pinch⅛ tsp¼ tsp⅜ tsp
Saltpinch⅛ tsp¼ tsp⅜ tsp

Steps

  1. Heat the oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add the onion, garlic, and ginger, cooking 8-10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until deeply softened.
  2. Add the collard greens in batches, stirring to wilt each addition before adding more.
  3. Stir in the cumin (if using) and a splash of water or stock. Cover and simmer 15-20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the greens are tender.
  4. Season with salt to taste. Serve warm, on its own or alongside Doro Wat or Key Wat.

Injera (Teff Sourdough Flatbread) (Bonus)

20 min (+45-60 min rise)MediumServes 1–4

Prep — Pouring Batter onto the Mitad

Ingredients by Serving (Weeknight-Shortcut Version)

Ingredient1234
Teff flour60g120g180g240g
All-purpose flour30g60g90g120g
Instant yeast⅛ tsp¼ tsp⅜ tsp½ tsp
Saltpinch⅛ tsp¼ tsp⅜ tsp
Warm water150ml300ml450ml600ml
Apple cider vinegar¼ tsp½ tsp¾ tsp1 tsp
Baking sodapinch⅛ tsp¼ tsp⅜ tsp
Vegetable oil or niter kibbeh10ml20ml30ml40ml

Steps

  1. Whisk the teff flour, all-purpose flour, yeast, and salt together in a large bowl.
  2. Add the warm water and whisk until you have a smooth, thin, pourable batter — thinner than pancake batter.
  3. Stir in the vinegar. Cover and let sit in a warm spot 45-60 minutes until bubbly on the surface (or refrigerate overnight for better flavor).
  4. Just before cooking, whisk in the baking soda for a last burst of bubbles.
  5. Heat a large nonstick skillet over medium heat and lightly oil it.
  6. Pour a thin, even layer of batter into the pan, swirling to coat the bottom.
  7. Cover and cook 2-3 minutes, undisturbed, until the surface is covered in small holes and the edges lift away from the pan. Do not flip.
  8. Slide onto a plate to cool. Repeat with the remaining batter, stacking cooked injera between layers of parchment or a clean towel.
  9. Serve at room temperature, torn into pieces, alongside the wats.
